s6_local-B2 — mf_composition / control-and-repair on the B1 defect-correction substrate —

2_motivation:
the batch has exactly one open surface and three preempted-but-owed controls, and
B1's own part 7 demands this batch ("s6-B2 should be a CONTROL-AND-REPAIR card on the same family,
not a new architecture, and it must carry the closed-form filter as a scored arm ... Do NOT spend a
batch on capacity, depth, receptive field or modes"). The open surface is verdict row (iii): "A
**data-driven, physics-free, per-SAMPLE scalar, fitted out-of-fold, deciding whether a
FIELD-VALUED defect corrector is applied at all, with the scored copy-LF field as the exact
fallback** appears in no fetched source." The other three arms are written as what the verdicts say
they are: a *reported floor* (row (i): "Claim **zero method novelty**; the contribution is the
*measured floor*"), a *cited bug fix* (row (ii): "hygiene, not a contribution ... Only reportable:
B1's *measurement* that zero padding held **45-81%** of a defect corrector's remaining squared
error in a 12-cell band ... plus the post-repair delta"), and a *control arm* (row (v): "**not a
novelty question**"). Two new read-only measurements I made justify the repair quantitatively:
the defect target `R` is boundary-**uniform** (12-cell band energy density ratio 1.043 / 1.045 /
1.041 / 1.024), so F10's 45-81% concentration is a model handicap; and `copylf_prediction`'s
`zoom(..., mode="nearest")` leaves copy-LF itself with a **4x wrap seam** (LF_up wrap ratio
3.89-4.18 vs HF 0.99-1.02) that zero padding forbids the corrector from seeing across.

Padding is switched by a **data-driven** criterion (ADR 0009-safe, no physics): circular iff the
HF-train wrap-continuity ratio `<= 1.25` on both axes (measured: pfc 1.015/0.991, allen_cahn
0.991/1.021, fisher_kpp 0.999/0.987, cahn_hilliard 1.000/1.000, helmholtz 0.348/0.859 -> circular;
heat_local 10.6/16.5, fluid 2.56/1.21 -> zeros). The trust head's features are `X` plus LF-field and
own-output statistics only (no PDE residual — ANCHOR is ADR-0009-disqualified), it is fitted on
`val_idx` which stages 0-2 never saw (Wolpert 1992, cited via https://arxiv.org/pdf/1106.1684), and
`alpha_hat = 0` reproduces copy-LF exactly. The Wolpert-fixed per-**pixel** training arm is
**dropped** (its ORACLE ceiling 4.1% / 1.2% / 0.6% / **-17%** is below every dataset's 10% relative
`min_claimable_effect`, and B1 F2 already ran the achievable val-fitted version) and replaced by a
free measurement-only out-of-fold pixel-map sidecar that carries no clause. Guard legs at 200
epochs for `circ_repair` and `lsi_ctrl`; one contract-tier (2-epoch) plumbing/no-harm screen over
all five arms on panel+guard whose numbers are never reportable (ADR 0007).

interpretation: THE INVERSION HAS A MECHANISM AND A PRE-REGISTRABLE PREDICTOR (confidence HIGH). The trained local corrector's value is a monotone function of how much of the defect R = HF - LF_up a single shift-invariant transfer function CANNOT explain (F5, Spearman -0.857, p = 0.014, n = 7), and that quantity survives cropping the boundary (F1). Where a closed form already explains >= 98.4% of the defect - all four sharp panel datasets - a 72k-parameter network has nothing left to win and loses on the rim; where it explains only 48-82% - the non-periodic guard set - the network converts the gap into a 3-17x score advantage. This retires 'does a local NEURAL operator have content?' as a PANEL question: on this panel the answer is arithmetically no, and that is a property of the datasets, not a modelling failure. It also gives the round a cheap pre-registration statistic: tools/defect_correction_learnability.py's rho_val_heldout, already promoted, is the number to read BEFORE spending a batch.

PERIODICITY IS THE WRONG QUESTION; THE RIGHT ONE IS WHETHER THE PADDING MATCHES THE BASE'S EXTENSION (confidence HIGH for the measurement, MEDIUM for the prescription). The card's data-driven switch measured HF-train wrap continuity, found 0.98-1.01, and chose circular - correctly, for the TARGET. But the corrector's INPUT is copylf_prediction's zoom(..., mode='nearest') upsample, whose wrap jump is 4x an interior jump on every panel dataset (F7). Circular padding therefore trades a zero-padding artifact for a seam-wrapping artifact and leaves a one-cell rim (F3) big enough to flip a pre-registered contrast (F8). The fix is not another padding mode: match the padding to the base's extension - i.e. correct a node-aligned / periodic base (tools/registration_audit.py variants C/D already construct one) or exclude a 1-cell rim from the corrector's loss. Neither was available to this card, whose base is frozen by the immutable eval layer.

THE TRUST HEAD IS A REUSABLE MECHANISM WITH ONE FIXABLE DEFECT AND ONE PRICED COST (confidence HIGH). It fits the per-sample optimum (F10), it is a self-diagnosis object keyed on its own correction's band profile and on LF amplitude rather than on X (F12), and it fires on exactly the amplitude / effective-N axis two other streams identified independently, capturing 59% of the oracle gain there. Its defect is a NORM mismatch: it regresses the L2-optimal alpha while the round scores relative L2 (F11). Its cost is that per-sample gating is not per-sample no-harm (F13). Both are addressable in the fitter, not the architecture.

cahn_hilliard's DEFECT IS DISPLACEMENT, AND THE DISPLACEMENT IS PER-SAMPLE (confidence MEDIUM-HIGH; the estimate is an oracle and a single rigid shift is a crude model of a probably space-varying warp). F9 + F14 together: large non-LSI defect share, val->test rho collapse on BOTH operator classes, exactly flat boundary profile, extra correction orthogonal to what remains, and a 2-dof-per-sample rigid shift oracle that beats both. It is the one panel dataset where additive local correction demonstrably saturates, and B1's hand-off to s3_warp is confirmed and sharpened.
